# Complex error function `cerf` and `cerfc` (DLMF §7.2)

We define the complex error function
`erf(z) = (2/√π) ∫_0^z e^{-u²} du = (2/√π) z ∫_0^1 e^{-(t z)²} dt`
and the complex complementary error function `erfc(z) = 1 - erf(z)`, as the
holomorphic extensions of the real `FLMF.Error.erf`/`FLMF.Error.erfc`.

Main results:

* `FLMF.Error.cerf_ofReal` : `cerf ↑x = ↑(erf x)` (agreement with the real `erf`).
* `FLMF.Error.cerfc_ofReal` : `cerfc ↑x = ↑(erfc x)`.
* `FLMF.Error.cerf_neg` : `cerf (-z) = - cerf z` (odd parity, DLMF 7.4.1).
* `FLMF.Error.cerf_zero` : `cerf 0 = 0`.

  surfaced).

# Repeated integrals of the complementary error function `iⁿerfc` (DLMF §7.18)

We define the `n`-fold repeated integral of `erfc`,
`iⁿerfc(x) = ∫ₓ^∞ i^{n-1}erfc(t) dt`, by recursion on `ℕ`:

`iRepErfc 0 x = erfc x`,
`iRepErfc (n+1) x = ∫_{(x,∞)} iRepErfc n t dt`   (DLMF 7.18.1, 7.18.2).

For the recursive integral to be meaningful we must know that each `iRepErfc n`
is integrable on every right half-line `Ioi x`.  The functions decay
super-exponentially; here we extract the (more than sufficient) uniform
exponential domination

`0 ≤ iRepErfc n t ≤ 3 · e^{-t}`   for `t ≥ 0`     (`iRepErfc_le_three_exp`),

which is *stable under the tail integral* — `∫_x^∞ 3 e^{-t} dt = 3 e^{-x}` — so a
single induction with a fixed constant carries the bound through every level.
Combined with continuity this gives integrability on all of `Ioi x`.

Main results:

* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc` — the repeated integral, defined by `ℕ`-recursion.
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_zero` — `i⁰erfc = erfc` (DLMF 7.18.1).
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_nonneg`, `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_le_three_exp` — nonnegativity
  and the uniform exponential bound on `[0, ∞)`.
* `FLMF.Error.continuous_iRepErfc`, `FLMF.Error.integrableOn_iRepErfc` — continuity
  and integrability on every `Ioi x`.
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_succ_eq` — one unfold of the defining recursion (the
  DLMF 7.18.2 closed form for all `n ≥ 0` is `erf_7_18_2` in `Ch7RepeatedErfc.lean`).
* `FLMF.Error.hasDerivAt_iRepErfc_succ` — the derivative relation
  `d/dx i^{n+1}erfc(x) = − iⁿerfc(x)` (DLMF 7.18.3).
* `FLMF.Error.deriv_iRepErfc_succ` — the same relation in `deriv` form.
* `FLMF.Error.tendsto_iRepErfc_atTop` — `iⁿerfc(t) → 0` as `t → +∞`.
* `FLMF.Error.erf_7_18_5` — the second-order ODE `W'' + 2z W' − 2n W = 0`
  (DLMF 7.18.5), for the general solution `W = A·iⁿerfc(z) + B·iⁿerfc(−z)`, `1 ≤ n`.
* `FLMF.Error.erf_7_18_7` — the three-term recurrence (DLMF 7.18.7).

# Repeated integrals of the complementary error function `iⁿerfc` (DLMF §7.18)

We define the `n`-fold repeated integral of `erfc`,
`iⁿerfc(x) = ∫ₓ^∞ i^{n-1}erfc(t) dt`, by recursion on `ℕ`:

`iRepErfc 0 x = erfc x`,
`iRepErfc (n+1) x = ∫_{(x,∞)} iRepErfc n t dt`   (DLMF 7.18.1, 7.18.2).

For the recursive integral to be meaningful we must know that each `iRepErfc n`
is integrable on every right half-line `Ioi x`.  The functions decay
super-exponentially; here we extract the (more than sufficient) uniform
exponential domination

`0 ≤ iRepErfc n t ≤ 3 · e^{-t}`   for `t ≥ 0`     (`iRepErfc_le_three_exp`),

which is *stable under the tail integral* — `∫_x^∞ 3 e^{-t} dt = 3 e^{-x}` — so a
single induction with a fixed constant carries the bound through every level.
Combined with continuity this gives integrability on all of `Ioi x`.

Main results:

* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc` — the repeated integral, defined by `ℕ`-recursion.
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_zero` — `i⁰erfc = erfc` (DLMF 7.18.1).
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_nonneg`, `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_le_three_exp` — nonnegativity
  and the uniform exponential bound on `[0, ∞)`.
* `FLMF.Error.continuous_iRepErfc`, `FLMF.Error.integrableOn_iRepErfc` — continuity
  and integrability on every `Ioi x`.
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_succ_eq` — one unfold of the defining recursion (the
  DLMF 7.18.2 closed form for all `n ≥ 0` is `erf_7_18_2` in `Ch7RepeatedErfc.lean`).
* `FLMF.Error.hasDerivAt_iRepErfc_succ` — the derivative relation
  `d/dx i^{n+1}erfc(x) = − iⁿerfc(x)` (DLMF 7.18.3).
* `FLMF.Error.deriv_iRepErfc_succ` — the same relation in `deriv` form.
* `FLMF.Error.tendsto_iRepErfc_atTop` — `iⁿerfc(t) → 0` as `t → +∞`.
* `FLMF.Error.erf_7_18_5` — the second-order ODE `W'' + 2z W' − 2n W = 0`
  (DLMF 7.18.5), for the general solution `W = A·iⁿerfc(z) + B·iⁿerfc(−z)`, `1 ≤ n`.
* `FLMF.Error.erf_7_18_7` — the three-term recurrence (DLMF 7.18.7).

# Repeated integrals of the complementary error function `iⁿerfc` (DLMF §7.18)

We define the `n`-fold repeated integral of `erfc`,
`iⁿerfc(x) = ∫ₓ^∞ i^{n-1}erfc(t) dt`, by recursion on `ℕ`:

`iRepErfc 0 x = erfc x`,
`iRepErfc (n+1) x = ∫_{(x,∞)} iRepErfc n t dt`   (DLMF 7.18.1, 7.18.2).

For the recursive integral to be meaningful we must know that each `iRepErfc n`
is integrable on every right half-line `Ioi x`.  The functions decay
super-exponentially; here we extract the (more than sufficient) uniform
exponential domination

`0 ≤ iRepErfc n t ≤ 3 · e^{-t}`   for `t ≥ 0`     (`iRepErfc_le_three_exp`),

which is *stable under the tail integral* — `∫_x^∞ 3 e^{-t} dt = 3 e^{-x}` — so a
single induction with a fixed constant carries the bound through every level.
Combined with continuity this gives integrability on all of `Ioi x`.

Main results:

* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc` — the repeated integral, defined by `ℕ`-recursion.
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_zero` — `i⁰erfc = erfc` (DLMF 7.18.1).
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_nonneg`, `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_le_three_exp` — nonnegativity
  and the uniform exponential bound on `[0, ∞)`.
* `FLMF.Error.continuous_iRepErfc`, `FLMF.Error.integrableOn_iRepErfc` — continuity
  and integrability on every `Ioi x`.
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_succ_eq` — one unfold of the defining recursion (the
  DLMF 7.18.2 closed form for all `n ≥ 0` is `erf_7_18_2` in `Ch7RepeatedErfc.lean`).
* `FLMF.Error.hasDerivAt_iRepErfc_succ` — the derivative relation
  `d/dx i^{n+1}erfc(x) = − iⁿerfc(x)` (DLMF 7.18.3).
* `FLMF.Error.deriv_iRepErfc_succ` — the same relation in `deriv` form.
* `FLMF.Error.tendsto_iRepErfc_atTop` — `iⁿerfc(t) → 0` as `t → +∞`.
* `FLMF.Error.erf_7_18_5` — the second-order ODE `W'' + 2z W' − 2n W = 0`
  (DLMF 7.18.5), for the general solution `W = A·iⁿerfc(z) + B·iⁿerfc(−z)`, `1 ≤ n`.
* `FLMF.Error.erf_7_18_7` — the three-term recurrence (DLMF 7.18.7).

`w(z) = e^{-z²} erfc(-iz)` is the scaled complex complementary error function

* 7.10.2 — first-order ODE `w' = -2z w + 2i/√π`  (surface)
* 7.10.3 — derivative recurrence  (surface)
* 7.19.3 — Voigt combination `U + iV` via `w`  (surface)

DLMF 7.9.3 (the continued fraction for `w`) remains a documented deferral: the
exact Gautschi partial-numerator pattern needs careful transcription that we did

Extra error-function entries that depend on the complex `cerf`/`cerfc` keystone,
the Faddeeva function `w`, and the continued-fraction machinery of §7.9:

# Repeated integrals of the complementary error function `iⁿerfc` (DLMF §7.18)

We define the `n`-fold repeated integral of `erfc`,
`iⁿerfc(x) = ∫ₓ^∞ i^{n-1}erfc(t) dt`, by recursion on `ℕ`:

`iRepErfc 0 x = erfc x`,
`iRepErfc (n+1) x = ∫_{(x,∞)} iRepErfc n t dt`   (DLMF 7.18.1, 7.18.2).

For the recursive integral to be meaningful we must know that each `iRepErfc n`
is integrable on every right half-line `Ioi x`.  The functions decay
super-exponentially; here we extract the (more than sufficient) uniform
exponential domination

`0 ≤ iRepErfc n t ≤ 3 · e^{-t}`   for `t ≥ 0`     (`iRepErfc_le_three_exp`),

which is *stable under the tail integral* — `∫_x^∞ 3 e^{-t} dt = 3 e^{-x}` — so a
single induction with a fixed constant carries the bound through every level.
Combined with continuity this gives integrability on all of `Ioi x`.

Main results:

* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc` — the repeated integral, defined by `ℕ`-recursion.
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_zero` — `i⁰erfc = erfc` (DLMF 7.18.1).
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_nonneg`, `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_le_three_exp` — nonnegativity
  and the uniform exponential bound on `[0, ∞)`.
* `FLMF.Error.continuous_iRepErfc`, `FLMF.Error.integrableOn_iRepErfc` — continuity
  and integrability on every `Ioi x`.
* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc_succ_eq` — one unfold of the defining recursion (the
  DLMF 7.18.2 closed form for all `n ≥ 0` is `erf_7_18_2` in `Ch7RepeatedErfc.lean`).
* `FLMF.Error.hasDerivAt_iRepErfc_succ` — the derivative relation
  `d/dx i^{n+1}erfc(x) = − iⁿerfc(x)` (DLMF 7.18.3).
* `FLMF.Error.deriv_iRepErfc_succ` — the same relation in `deriv` form.
* `FLMF.Error.tendsto_iRepErfc_atTop` — `iⁿerfc(t) → 0` as `t → +∞`.

# Limits of the Fresnel integrals at `+∞` (DLMF §7.12)

The Fresnel integrals satisfy `C(x) → 1/2` and `S(x) → 1/2` as `x → +∞`
(DLMF 7.2.7 in conjunction with the normalization `C(∞) = S(∞) = 1/2`,
DLMF 7.5.1).

This module proves the **convergence half** of that statement, sorry-free:
`C` and `S` each converge at `+∞` to *some* real limit
(`exists_tendsto_fresnelC`, `exists_tendsto_fresnelS`). The mechanism is the
oscillatory-tail (non-stationary-phase) bound

`|∫ₐᵇ cos(πt²/2) dt| ≤ 3/(π a)`  (and the same for `sin`),  for `0 < a ≤ b`,

obtained by one integration by parts (`u = 1/(πt)`, `dv = d sin(πt²/2)`),
exactly mirroring `FLMF/Functions/ExpIntegrals/SiLeading.lean`'s
`abs_integral_sin_div_le` for `Si`. The tail bound makes `C` and `S` Cauchy at
`atTop`, hence convergent in the complete space `ℝ`.

It also records, sorry-free, the **Abel value** of the (full-line) regularized
Fresnel Gaussian: with the DLMF phase `a = π/2`,

`lim_{ε↓0} ∫_ℝ e^{-(ε - i(π/2))x²} dx = (2i)^{1/2} = 1 + i`   (`abel_value_eq`),

via `FLMF.Methods.StationaryPhase.fresnel_regularized` and
`cpow_half_pos_mul_I`. Its real/imaginary parts are `1` (full line), i.e. `1/2`
on the half line `(0,∞)` — the conjectured limit values of `C` and `S`.

## Value identification (`L_C = L_S = 1/2`)

The limits are pinned to `1/2` via the **Abelian bridge**
(`tendsto_fresnelC`, `tendsto_fresnelS`), sorry-free. Two ingredients combine:

1. **Abelian–Gaussian** (`FLMF.Methods.AbelianGaussian.abelian_gaussian`): the
   improper convergence `∫_0^R cosArg → L_C` (the convergence half above) implies
   the Gaussian-regularized half-line value
   `lim_{ε↓0} ∫_{(0,∞)} e^{-εt²} cosArg = L_C` (likewise for `sinArg`/`L_S`).

2. **Regularized full-line Fresnel Gaussian**
   (`FLMF.Methods.StationaryPhase.fresnel_regularized` with `a = π/2`):
   `lim_{ε↓0} ∫_ℝ e^{-(ε - i(π/2))x²} dx = (2i)^{1/2} = 1 + i` (`abel_value_eq`).
   Taking real/imaginary parts and using the integrand's evenness
   (`integral_comp_abs`) gives `2·lim_{ε↓0} ∫_{(0,∞)} e^{-εt²} cosArg = 1` and
   `2·lim_{ε↓0} ∫_{(0,∞)} e^{-εt²} sinArg = 1`.

Uniqueness of limits then forces `L_C = L_S = 1/2`, hence
`C(x) → 1/2` and `S(x) → 1/2` as `x → +∞` (DLMF 7.5.1).

# Limits of the Fresnel integrals at `+∞` (DLMF §7.12)

The Fresnel integrals satisfy `C(x) → 1/2` and `S(x) → 1/2` as `x → +∞`
(DLMF 7.2.7 in conjunction with the normalization `C(∞) = S(∞) = 1/2`,
DLMF 7.5.1).

This module proves the **convergence half** of that statement, sorry-free:
`C` and `S` each converge at `+∞` to *some* real limit
(`exists_tendsto_fresnelC`, `exists_tendsto_fresnelS`). The mechanism is the
oscillatory-tail (non-stationary-phase) bound

`|∫ₐᵇ cos(πt²/2) dt| ≤ 3/(π a)`  (and the same for `sin`),  for `0 < a ≤ b`,

obtained by one integration by parts (`u = 1/(πt)`, `dv = d sin(πt²/2)`),
exactly mirroring `FLMF/Functions/ExpIntegrals/SiLeading.lean`'s
`abs_integral_sin_div_le` for `Si`. The tail bound makes `C` and `S` Cauchy at
`atTop`, hence convergent in the complete space `ℝ`.

It also records, sorry-free, the **Abel value** of the (full-line) regularized
Fresnel Gaussian: with the DLMF phase `a = π/2`,

`lim_{ε↓0} ∫_ℝ e^{-(ε - i(π/2))x²} dx = (2i)^{1/2} = 1 + i`   (`abel_value_eq`),

via `FLMF.Methods.StationaryPhase.fresnel_regularized` and
`cpow_half_pos_mul_I`. Its real/imaginary parts are `1` (full line), i.e. `1/2`
on the half line `(0,∞)` — the conjectured limit values of `C` and `S`.

## Value identification (`L_C = L_S = 1/2`)

The limits are pinned to `1/2` via the **Abelian bridge**
(`tendsto_fresnelC`, `tendsto_fresnelS`), sorry-free. Two ingredients combine:

1. **Abelian–Gaussian** (`FLMF.Methods.AbelianGaussian.abelian_gaussian`): the
   improper convergence `∫_0^R cosArg → L_C` (the convergence half above) implies
   the Gaussian-regularized half-line value
   `lim_{ε↓0} ∫_{(0,∞)} e^{-εt²} cosArg = L_C` (likewise for `sinArg`/`L_S`).

2. **Regularized full-line Fresnel Gaussian**
   (`FLMF.Methods.StationaryPhase.fresnel_regularized` with `a = π/2`):
   `lim_{ε↓0} ∫_ℝ e^{-(ε - i(π/2))x²} dx = (2i)^{1/2} = 1 + i` (`abel_value_eq`).
   Taking real/imaginary parts and using the integrand's evenness
   (`integral_comp_abs`) gives `2·lim_{ε↓0} ∫_{(0,∞)} e^{-εt²} cosArg = 1` and
   `2·lim_{ε↓0} ∫_{(0,∞)} e^{-εt²} sinArg = 1`.

Uniqueness of limits then forces `L_C = L_S = 1/2`, hence
`C(x) → 1/2` and `S(x) → 1/2` as `x → +∞` (DLMF 7.5.1).

For any natural number $n$ and complex number $z$ such that the absolute value of the principal argument of $z$ is strictly less than $\pi/4$, we have

# DLMF §7.5 — Interrelations

Statement surfaces (Phase 5) for the §7.5 "Interrelations" identities, which
relate `erf`/`erfc`, Dawson's integral `F`, the Fresnel integrals `C`, `S`, and
their auxiliary functions `f`, `g`.

FLMF's `erf`, `erfc`, `dawson`, and the Fresnel `C`, `S` are all **real-valued**.
Several §7.5 identities are intrinsically complex — they involve the complex
Fresnel function `𝓕(z) = ½(1+i) - (C(z) + iS(z))` (7.5.2), the Faddeeva function
`w(z)`, the complex variable `ζ = ½√π(1∓i)z` (7.5.7), or the complex auxiliary
combination `g(z) ± if(z)`. Those are recorded below as **documented deferrals**
rather than faked.

* 7.5.1  — Dawson's integral against the Faddeeva function and `erf` is proven at DLMF's
  full complex strength as `erf_7_5_1` (the complex `cdawson` from `ComplexErfExtra.lean`,
  `faddeeva`, `cerf`); the display is an equality chain, so the surface is the single
  two-conjunct theorem required by the chain-display convention.

* 7.5.3  — the `C(z)` reconstruction from the auxiliary `f`, `g` is proven at DLMF's
  full complex strength as `cfresnel_7_5_3`, the exact companion of `cfresnel_7_5_4`.

* 7.5.4  — the `S(z)` reconstruction from the auxiliary `f`, `g` is proven at DLMF's
  full complex strength as `cfresnel_7_5_4` (using the complex `cfresnelS`,
  `cfresnelAuxF`, `cfresnelAuxG` from `Fresnel/Complex.lean`); `erf_7_5_4` keeps the
  real specialization as a non-DLMF-tagged convenience lemma.

The remaining identities with honest real specializations are:

* 7.5.11 — `|𝓕(x)|² = f²(x) + g²(x)` for `x ≥ 0`, read as the real identity
  `(½ - C x)² + (½ - S x)² = f(x)² + g(x)²`;
* 7.5.12 — its `x ≤ 0` counterpart.

The auxiliary functions are defined here inline by their DLMF §7.2 formulas
(7.2.10, 7.2.11), which are real-valued in terms of the real `C`, `S`.

* 7.5.13 — the Goodwin–Staton integral `G(x) = √π·F(x) - ½e^{-x²}Ei(x²)` for `x > 0`.

All surfaces stated in this file are proven.

# Continued-fraction expansions for `erfc` (DLMF §7.9)

Statement surfaces for the Laplace continued-fraction expansions of the
complementary error function (DLMF §7.9).

DLMF §7.9 records three continued fractions:

* **7.9.1** `√π e^{z²} erfc(z) = z / (z² + ½ / (1 + 1 / (z² + 3/2 / (1 + ⋯))))`,
* **7.9.2** `√π e^{z²} erfc(z) = 2z / (2z² + 1 − 1·2 / (2z² + 5 − 3·4 / (2z² + 9 − ⋯)))`,
  the *even part* of (7.9.1), and
* **7.9.3** a continued fraction for the Faddeeva function `w(z)`.

A continued fraction is faithfully stated as the **limit of its convergents**:
we build the partial numerators/denominators `A n`, `B n` of the truncated
fraction via the standard Wallis (fundamental) recurrence and state that the
convergents `A n / B n` tend to the function value as `n → ∞`.

For each of 7.9.1/7.9.2 we surface two theorems:

* `erf_7_9_1`/`erf_7_9_2`: the REAL-argument specialization (`x > 0`), proven
  in full via the real Gaussian-tail-integral (`erfJ`) route — this is exactly
  the `z ∈ (0,∞)` slice of the DLMF identities (valid on `ℜ z > 0`);
* `erf_7_9_1_complex`/`erf_7_9_2_complex`: the DLMF-faithful full-strength
  statement for complex `z` with `ℜ z > 0`, using the complex `cerfc` of
  `FLMF.Functions.Error.ComplexErf`.  The real proof's tail-positivity
  argument does not transfer to the complex domain; instead these are proven
  from the complex tail integrals `Kₙ(z) = ∫₀^∞ sⁿ e^{-s²-2zs} ds` (whose
  `n = 0` value is the Laplace-transform representation DLMF 7.7.3 of `erfc`),
  which give the *exact remainder* of the fraction, combined with Van Vleck's
  sector convergence theorem (`FLMF.Methods.VanVleck`, DLMF 1.12.28) applied to

# Continued-fraction expansions for `erfc` (DLMF §7.9)

Statement surfaces for the Laplace continued-fraction expansions of the
complementary error function (DLMF §7.9).

DLMF §7.9 records three continued fractions:

* **7.9.1** `√π e^{z²} erfc(z) = z / (z² + ½ / (1 + 1 / (z² + 3/2 / (1 + ⋯))))`,
* **7.9.2** `√π e^{z²} erfc(z) = 2z / (2z² + 1 − 1·2 / (2z² + 5 − 3·4 / (2z² + 9 − ⋯)))`,
  the *even part* of (7.9.1), and
* **7.9.3** a continued fraction for the Faddeeva function `w(z)`.

A continued fraction is faithfully stated as the **limit of its convergents**:
we build the partial numerators/denominators `A n`, `B n` of the truncated
fraction via the standard Wallis (fundamental) recurrence and state that the
convergents `A n / B n` tend to the function value as `n → ∞`.

For each of 7.9.1/7.9.2 we surface two theorems:

* `erf_7_9_1`/`erf_7_9_2`: the REAL-argument specialization (`x > 0`), proven
  in full via the real Gaussian-tail-integral (`erfJ`) route — this is exactly
  the `z ∈ (0,∞)` slice of the DLMF identities (valid on `ℜ z > 0`);
* `erf_7_9_1_complex`/`erf_7_9_2_complex`: the DLMF-faithful full-strength
  statement for complex `z` with `ℜ z > 0`, using the complex `cerfc` of
  `FLMF.Functions.Error.ComplexErf`.  The real proof's tail-positivity
  argument does not transfer to the complex domain; instead these are proven
  from the complex tail integrals `Kₙ(z) = ∫₀^∞ sⁿ e^{-s²-2zs} ds` (whose
  `n = 0` value is the Laplace-transform representation DLMF 7.7.3 of `erfc`),
  which give the *exact remainder* of the fraction, combined with Van Vleck's
  sector convergence theorem (`FLMF.Methods.VanVleck`, DLMF 1.12.28) applied to
  the `aₙ ↦ 1` normalization of the fraction.  See the section "The complex
  tail integrals of the DLMF 7.9.1 fraction" below.

7.9.3 is the Faddeeva function `w(z)`, which is complex-valued and not provided
by FLMF; it is recorded as a documented deferral below.

# Leading asymptotics of the complementary error function `erfc`

We work with the Watson-ready representation
`erfc(x) = (2/√π) · e^{-x²} ∫_{(0,∞)} e^{-(2x) u} · e^{-u²} du`,
obtained from `erfc(x) = (2/√π) ∫_x^∞ e^{-t²} dt` by the substitution

`erfc(x) ~ e^{-x²}/(x √π)` then follows from the leading-order Watson lemma
`PicardLefschetz.watson_leading` with `s = 1`, parameter `2x`,
`g(u) = e^{-u²}` and `a₀ = g(0⁺) = 1`.

`erfc` itself is the canonical `1 - erf` of `FLMF.Functions.Error.Erf`; the
Watson-ready form is recorded here as the theorem `erfc_eq_watson`.

* `FLMF.Error.erfc_eq_watson` — the Watson-ready (`t = x + u`) integral form.

functions `erf`/`erfc` and the Fresnel integrals `C`/`S` to the incomplete gamma
function, the confluent hypergeometric functions (Kummer `M`, Tricomi `U`), and
the Gauss hypergeometric function `₂F₁`.

principal branch (`cerf_7_11_1`, `cerfc_7_11_2`, `cerf_7_11_3`), using the
complex incomplete-gamma module `FLMF.Functions.IncompleteGamma.ComplexDef`
(`clowerGamma`, `cupperGamma`, `cexpIntegralE`); the real-`z` forms below are
demoted to `-- no-dlmf` restrictions.  Each complex surface carries the sector

half-plane, so `Re z > 0` is the maximal true principal-branch domain (DLMF
states them unrestricted because its `γ`, `Γ`, `E_p` are the continued,
multivalued objects — the displays are branch-implicit).  See the `ComplexDef`

# Full asymptotic series for the complementary error function `erfc`

Continuing from `FLMF.Functions.Error.ErfcLeading`, we use the Watson-ready
representation
`erfc(x) = (2/√π) · e^{-x²} ∫_{(0,∞)} e^{-(2x) u} · e^{-u²} du`
and the full `N`-term Watson series lemma `PicardLefschetz.watson_series`
(with `s = 1` and amplitude `g(u) = e^{-u²}`) to obtain the asymptotic
expansion of `erfc` (DLMF §7.12.1).

The amplitude has the convergent Taylor expansion
`e^{-u²} = Σ_{k} ((-1)^k / k!) u^{2k}`, but for `watson_series` we only need a
finite split with a *bounded* remainder `h`:
`g u = Σ_{k<N} a k · u^k + u^N · h u`.

We package the general engine `erfc_watson_series`, which produces the full
asymptotic series of `erfc` (DLMF §7.12.1).

* `cerf_eq_tsum` — **DLMF 7.6.1** at its stated strength: the Maclaurin series
  `erf z = (2/√π) ∑ (−1)ⁿ z^(2n+1) / (n!(2n+1))`, for all complex `z`.

  computation underneath it.
* `erf_7_11_4` — **DLMF 7.11.4** at its stated strength: the two-member chain
  `erf z = (2z/√π) M(1/2, 3/2, −z²) = (2z/√π) e^{−z²} M(1, 3/2, z²)`, for all
  complex `z`. `cerf_eq_kummerM` / `cerf_eq_kummerM_transform` are its links and
  `erf_eq_kummerM` is the real specialization, kept as proven infrastructure.
  (This identity is DLMF 7.11.4, NOT 7.6.2: 7.6.2 is the *series*
  `erf z = (2/√π) e^{−z²} ∑ 2ⁿ z^{2n+1}/(1·3⋯(2n+1))`, which FLMF does not
  currently state.)

The gaussian `e^{−t²}` is expanded into its exponential series inside the
defining integral; the termwise pieces are polynomials `t^{2n}`, so the
sum–integral interchange (norm-integrals dominated by `(d−c)·(R²)ⁿ/n!` on

interval. The Kummer series is matched through the coefficient collapse
`cₙ(1/2, 3/2) = 1/((2n+1)·n!)`. The complex surfaces run the same expansion
along `cerf`'s defining ray integral `∫₀¹ z·e^{−(tz)²} dt` (real `t ∈ [0,1]`,
complex constant `z`).

# Complex Fresnel integrals `cfresnelC` and `cfresnelS` (DLMF §7.2)

We define the complex Fresnel cosine and sine integrals
`C(z) = ∫₀ᶻ cos(πu²/2) du = z ∫₀¹ cos(π(t z)²/2) dt` and
`S(z) = ∫₀ᶻ sin(πu²/2) du = z ∫₀¹ sin(π(t z)²/2) dt`, as the entire
extensions of the real `FLMF.Fresnel.fresnelC`/`FLMF.Fresnel.fresnelS`.

Main results:

* `FLMF.Fresnel.cfresnelC_ofReal` : `cfresnelC ↑x = ↑(fresnelC x)` (agreement).
* `FLMF.Fresnel.cfresnelS_ofReal` : `cfresnelS ↑x = ↑(fresnelS x)` (agreement).
* `FLMF.Fresnel.cfresnelC_neg` / `cfresnelS_neg` : odd parity (DLMF 7.4.5).
* `FLMF.Fresnel.cfresnelC_zero` / `cfresnelS_zero` : values at `0`.

This file is the statement surface for DLMF §7.17 "Inverse Error Functions"
(equations 7.17.1–7.17.6, plus the coefficient recursion 7.17.2_5).

# Repeated integrals of the complementary error function `iⁿerfc` (DLMF §7.18)

We define the `n`-fold repeated integral of `erfc`,
`iⁿerfc(x) = ∫ₓ^∞ i^{n-1}erfc(t) dt`, by recursion on `ℕ`:

`iRepErfc 0 x = erfc x`,
`iRepErfc (n+1) x = ∫_{(x,∞)} iRepErfc n t dt`   (DLMF 7.18.1, 7.18.2).

For the recursive integral to be meaningful we must know that each `iRepErfc n`
is integrable on every right half-line `Ioi x`.  The functions decay
super-exponentially; here we extract the (more than sufficient) uniform
exponential domination

`0 ≤ iRepErfc n t ≤ 3 · e^{-t}`   for `t ≥ 0`     (`iRepErfc_le_three_exp`),

which is *stable under the tail integral* — `∫_x^∞ 3 e^{-t} dt = 3 e^{-x}` — so a
single induction with a fixed constant carries the bound through every level.
Combined with continuity this gives integrability on all of `Ioi x`.

* `FLMF.Error.iRepErfc` — the repeated integral, defined by `ℕ`-recursion.

# Limits of the Fresnel integrals at `+∞` (DLMF §7.12)

The Fresnel integrals satisfy `C(x) → 1/2` and `S(x) → 1/2` as `x → +∞`
(DLMF 7.2.7 in conjunction with the normalization `C(∞) = S(∞) = 1/2`,
DLMF 7.5.1).

This module proves the **convergence half** of that statement, sorry-free:
`C` and `S` each converge at `+∞` to *some* real limit
(`exists_tendsto_fresnelC`, `exists_tendsto_fresnelS`). The mechanism is the
oscillatory-tail (non-stationary-phase) bound

`|∫ₐᵇ cos(πt²/2) dt| ≤ 3/(π a)`  (and the same for `sin`),  for `0 < a ≤ b`,

obtained by one integration by parts (`u = 1/(πt)`, `dv = d sin(πt²/2)`),
exactly mirroring `FLMF/Functions/ExpIntegrals/SiLeading.lean`'s
`abs_integral_sin_div_le` for `Si`. The tail bound makes `C` and `S` Cauchy at
`atTop`, hence convergent in the complete space `ℝ`.

It also records, sorry-free, the **Abel value** of the (full-line) regularized
Fresnel Gaussian: with the DLMF phase `a = π/2`,

`lim_{ε↓0} ∫_ℝ e^{-(ε - i(π/2))x²} dx = (2i)^{1/2} = 1 + i`   (`abel_value_eq`),

via `FLMF.Methods.StationaryPhase.fresnel_regularized` and
`cpow_half_pos_mul_I`. Its real/imaginary parts are `1` (full line), i.e. `1/2`
on the half line `(0,∞)` — the conjectured limit values of `C` and `S`.

and the complementary error function `erfc(x) = 1 - erf(x)`, reusing Mathlib's

rather than faked.

# The repeated integrals of `erfc` for a complex variable (DLMF §7.18)

DLMF §7.18 assigns its variable `z` the *complex* domain throughout, while
`FLMF.Error.iRepErfc : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ` (`RepeatedErfc.lean`) is the real-axis
object built by iterated Lebesgue tail integrals.  This module supplies the
complex twin and re-surfaces the §7.18 displays over `ℂ`.

The complex definition is the **horizontal-ray Laplace form** of the closed
integral representation 7.18.2, i.e. the substitution `t = z + s` in
`iⁿerfc(z) = (2/√π) ∫_z^∞ (t−z)ⁿ/n! · e^{−t²} dt`:

`iⁿerfc(z) = (2/√π) ∫_0^∞ (sⁿ/n!) e^{−(z+s)²} ds`   (`cRepErfc`).

No sector hypothesis is needed: `‖e^{−(z+s)²}‖ = e^{(Im z)² − (Re z + s)²}`
decays like `e^{−s²/2}` for every fixed `z`, locally uniformly, so the integral
converges on all of `ℂ` and `cRepErfc n` is entire
(`differentiable_cRepErfc`, via `FLMF.Methods.analyticOnNhd_integral_of_locallyDominated`).

Agreement with the real family (`cRepErfc_ofReal`) plus entirety then transfers
every §7.18 polynomial identity from the real axis by the identity theorem
(`FLMF.Methods.eqOn_of_entire_of_eqOn_real`).

Main results:

* `FLMF.Error.cRepErfc`, `cRepErfcNegOne`, `cRepErfcPred` — the complex family,
  its `n = −1` member, and the `n − 1` index shift.
* `FLMF.Error.cRepErfc_ofReal` — `iⁿerfc` on `ℝ` is the restriction of `cRepErfc`.
* `FLMF.Error.differentiable_cRepErfc` — `cRepErfc n` is entire.
* `FLMF.Error.HhC` — the complex probability function `Hhₙ`, with
  `HhC_ofReal` / `differentiable_HhC`.
* `FLMF.Error.cerf_7_18_1`, `cerf_7_18_2`, `cerf_7_18_3`, `cerf_7_18_4`,
  `cerf_7_18_5`, `cerf_7_18_6`, `cerf_7_18_7`, `cerf_7_18_8`, `cerf_7_18_11`,
  `cerf_7_18_12` — the complex-variable surfaces of the corresponding DLMF
  displays.  The real statements of `RepeatedErfc.lean` /
  `Ch7RepeatedErfc.lean` are their real-axis restrictions.

Two of the displays are also *index-repaired* here: `cerf_7_18_3` and
`cerf_7_18_7` are stated through `cRepErfcPred`, so they cover DLMF's lowest
index (`n = 0`, resp. `m = 1`), which the real `ℕ`-shifted statements omitted.

# The DLMF 7.18.13 continued fraction over `ℂ` (`ℜ z > 0`)

DLMF 7.18.13 expands the ratio of consecutive repeated integrals of the
complementary error function as a continued fraction
```
  iⁿerfc(z)/i^{n−1}erfc(z) = (1/2)/(z + ((n+1)/2)/(z + ((n+2)/2)/(z + ⋯))),
```
valid for every `n = 0, 1, 2, …` and every **complex** `z` with `ℜ z > 0` (for
`n = 0` the denominator is the base member `i^{−1}erfc(z) = (2/√π)e^{−z²}` of
DLMF 7.18.1, which is `cRepErfcPred 0`).

`FLMF.Error.erf_7_18_13_general` proves the **real** slice `0 < z` of this
display; its convergence engine (`FLMF.Methods.tendsto_convs_of_tails`) is the
Stieltjes even/odd sandwich and is intrinsically real.  This file carries the
complex statement, on the three ingredients

1. **Convergence** (proven, `cerfcCF_exists_tendsto`).  The fraction has
   positive real partial numerators `1/2, (n+1)/2, (n+2)/2, …` and the constant
   partial denominator `z` in the open right half-plane, so it is exactly the
   shape covered by the sector criterion
   `FLMF.Methods.PosNumSector.exists_tendsto_convs_const` (an equivalence
   transformation to all-ones partial numerators followed by Van Vleck's
   theorem, DLMF 1.12.28).  The same criterion gives that the continuant
   denominators never vanish (`cerfcCF_dens_ne_zero`), which is what makes the
   convergents well defined on `ℜ z > 0`.

2. **The exact remainder** (proven, `cerfcCF_remainder`).  Writing
   `Uⱼ = i^{n+j−1}erfc(z)` (so `U₀ = i^{n−1}erfc(z)`, `U₁ = iⁿerfc(z)`), DLMF
   7.18.7 reads `2(n+j+1)U_{j+2} = Uⱼ − 2z U_{j+1}`, and a two-step induction
   against the Wallis recurrence gives the closed form
   ```
     U₁ Bₘ − U₀ Aₘ = (−1)ᵐ (∏_{k=1}^m (n+k)) U_{m+1}
   ```
   for the continuants `Aₘ = cfNumC`, `Bₘ = cfDenC` of the fraction.  This is
   the complex counterpart of the real proof's exact-tail factorization: the
   right-hand side is the *minimal* solution of the three-term recurrence, the
   continuants are dominant solutions, and the fraction converges to `U₁/U₀`
   exactly when the ratio of the two tends to `0`.

3. **The limit identification** (open, `cerfcCF_remainder_div_dens_tendsto_zero`
   together with `cRepErfcPred_ne_zero_of_re_pos`).  See the docstrings of those
   two lemmas for the precise mathematical content of each gap.

# The four-term asymptotic expansion of `inverfc` (DLMF 7.17.3)

`FLMF/Functions/Error/Ch7InverseErf.lean` proves only the **leading term** of DLMF
7.17.3 (`inverfc x · √u → 1`, i.e. `inverfc x - u^{-1/2} = o(u^{-1/2})`).  This file
carries the faithful, four-term display

`inverfc x ∼ u^{-1/2} + a₂ u^{3/2} + a₃ u^{5/2} + a₄ u^{7/2}`  (`x → 0⁺`),

with `u = asymU x` (DLMF 7.17.5) and `a_k = asymA x k` (DLMF 7.17.4), as the Poincaré
truncation `erf_7_17_3_full`.

## The route: log-log asymptotic inversion

Put `y = inverfc x`, so `erfc y = x` and `y → ∞` as `x → 0⁺`.  Everything is driven by
one **exact** identity.  Write

* `M y = √π · y · e^{y²} · erfc y`  (`erfcMills`, the normalized Mills factor; `M → 1`),
* `L y = ln (1 / erfc y)`  (`= ln(1/x)`),
* `A y = ln y + ½ ln π - ln (M y)`  (`inverfcAuxA`), so that `L y = y² + A y` exactly,
* `W y = ln (L y) - 2 ln y = ln (L y / y²)`  (`inverfcAuxW`), so `W y = ln (1 + A y / y²)`,
* `S y = y² - (asymU (erfc y))⁻¹`  (`inverfcAuxS`), the *inversion gap*.

Unfolding `asymU` (7.17.5) and `asymV` (7.17.6) along `x = erfc y` gives

* `(asymU (erfc y))⁻¹ = L y - ½ ln π - ½ ln (L y)`   (`asymU_erfc_inv_eq`), hence
* `S y = ln (M y) + ½ W y`                            (`inverfcAuxS_eq`),
* `asymV (erfc y) = W y + 2 ln y - 2 + ln π`          (`asymV_erfc_eq`).

The second-order `erfc` expansion (`erfc_7_12_1 1`, i.e. `M y = 1 - 1/(2y²) + o(y^{-2})`)
gives `y² ln (M y) → -½`; combined with `y² W y - A y → 0` this yields the **first
bootstrap step**

`y² · S y - asymV (erfc y) / 4 → 0`   (`tendsto_sq_mul_inverfcAuxS_sub`),

which is exactly `S = (v/4) u + o(u)`, the second order of the inversion.  (The `-2` in
DLMF's `v = ln ln(1/x) - 2 + ln π` is precisely the `-1/(2y²)` term of the `erfc`
expansion; that is the sense in which 7.17.6 is the *second* term of the inversion.)

The passage from the gap `S` to the display is the exact algebraic identity
`P - 1 = ½(P² - 1) - ½(P - 1)²` for `P = y √u` (see `normalized_gap_identity`).
